headline: Bone Age Explained
subhead: AND WHY IT IS MEASURED FROM THE WRONG BONES

headline: Covering the Basics:
body: Bone age is assessed from a radiograph of the hand and wrist, comparing the appearance of the carpal bones and phalangeal growth plates to a reference atlas. The resulting number is then used to estimate remaining growth potential for the whole skeleton. | This assumes that the maturation state of the hand reflects the maturation state of the long bones, (which, as the data below shows, it does not).
punch: The hand is used as a proxy for the legs.

headline: Differential Growth Plate Senescence
body: Growth plates in different bones do not share one clock. In mice, *epiphyseal fusion*, defined as disappearance of the growth plate, occurred at approximately **3 weeks** in phalanges and **4 weeks** in metacarpals, but had not yet occurred at **12 weeks** in tibias or femurs. | The same order was observed in rats: **12 weeks** in phalanges, **16 weeks** in metacarpals, with tibias and femurs still open at 16 weeks.
punch: _Small bones fuse first in both species examined._

headline: Growth Rate Differences
body: At one week of age, the metacarpal bone growth rate was **49%** of the tibial rate, and the *chondrocyte proliferation rate per column* was **46%** of the tibial value. | All structural and functional markers of *growth plate senescence*, the progressive decline in proliferative capacity, were more advanced in the metacarpals and proximal phalanges compared with the distal femurs and proximal tibias.
punch: ==The hand bones grow at roughly half the rate and senesce earlier.==

headline: IGF Signalling's Role
body: Chondrocytes isolated from phalanges and metacarpals proliferated less than those from tibias and femurs. Addition of IGF-1 to the culture medium increased proliferation of the phalangeal/metacarpal chondrocytes **to match that of untreated tibial/femoral chondrocytes**. | This indicates the difference lies in local IGF signalling rather than an intrinsic property of the cells, (consistent with the higher IGFBP expression the authors report in the smaller bones).
punch: The bone is equivalent. The local signalling is not.

headline: Human Data
body: A cross-sectional MRI study of **958 subjects** aged 14 to 21, imaging the wrist, knee and ankle in each participant. Fusion timing varied by site within the same individual, and complete fusion occurred approximately **2 years earlier** in females than males. | *Pubertal development* (Tanner stage) correlated with growth plate fusion at every site: **0.514 to 0.598** in males, 0.287 to 0.513 in females.
punch: _One individual, several closure dates, all tracked by pubertal stage._

headline: Physical Activity vs BMI
body: **BMI** correlated with growth plate maturity, 0.186 to 0.384, higher in males. **Physical activity** showed no significant correlation in males at any site, and in females only a very low correlation at the distal radius (**0.095**), with no other site reaching significance. | Body composition, not training load, was the variable associated with faster maturation in this dataset.
punch: ==Training did not track plate maturity. BMI did.==

headline: Practical Application
subhead: HOW TO READ YOUR OWN NUMBER
body: Interpret bone age as an estimate derived from the fastest-maturing bones in the body, not as a direct readout of long bone status. Track pubertal stage, which correlated with fusion at every site imaged. | Coaching and sources in bio.
punch: The hand matures first, in every dataset examined.
